description: Shared capabilities every spawned CodeTerm agent receives before its role and assignment.

evals.name: rich-workflow-visualization
evals.prompt: Without running commands, briefly explain which native CodeTerm rendering formats you would use for a workflow visualization and when inline HTML is appropriate.
evals.expected_output: Knows the shared rich-rendering contract available to every spawned CodeTerm agent.
expectations: Identifies Mermaid and a self-contained sandboxed HTML block as workflow visualization options
States that inline HTML is only for light native markup

evals.name: sandboxed-html-runtime
evals.prompt: Without running commands, briefly describe how you would directly render an animated interactive HTML status card in CodeTerm. Also say what you would do only if the card later needed an unfamiliar CodeTerm-specific runtime capability or a local file chosen by the user.
evals.expected_output: Knows the safe self-contained HTML runtime without assuming network or arbitrary filesystem access.
expectations: States that bundled Tailwind utilities are available for layout, interaction states, transitions, or animations
Uses ct.help() only when an unfamiliar CodeTerm-specific runtime capability is actually needed
Uses ct.file.pick() only for an explicitly user-selected local file
Does NOT claim direct network or arbitrary filesystem access

evals.name: file-backed-html-render
evals.prompt: You created C:\Users\User\Desktop\design-system.html and the user wants that exact file to be the single source rendered in the current CodeTerm reply. Show the minimal reply syntax. Do not copy the file contents.
evals.expected_output: Uses the file-backed HTML fence rather than duplicating the file or asking the user to pick it.
expectations: Includes an html fence whose entire body is @file C:\Users\User\Desktop\design-system.html
Does NOT copy or paraphrase the HTML file contents
Does NOT use ct.file.pick() or ct.file.renderHtml() for a known file path
